key_points: Original request (CL-01, stakeholder SH-CX): build a chatbot explaining to customers why parcels are late. The defined root problem (PD-1) is that 300 of 1000 orders (30%) are flagged late at the 'handover' stage (E-01), traced to the warehouse RELEASE-BATCH job failing in 21 of 30 runs, with 290 orders marked released only after the carrier already picked them up (E-04).

The problem definition was established by testing competing hypotheses: a carrier-scheduling cause (H-CARRIER-PICKUP-SCHEDULING, backed by stakeholder claim E-03 and pickup data E-02/E-06) was REJECTED because it is contradicted by E-04; a pure customer-communication-gap explanation (H-CUSTOMER-COMM-GAP) was also REJECTED (contradicted by E-01, E-02, E-03, E-04). Warehouse-processing-delay (H-WAREHOUSE-PROCESSING-DELAY) and handoff-failure (H-HANDOFF-FAILURE) hypotheses remain SUPPORTED by E-04 and E-01.

The DEFINE gate result was CONDITIONAL_PASS, deferring the critical unknown of whether the 290 released-after-pickup orders (E-04) are the same orders as the 300 handover-late orders (E-01); this was tracked as VOB-U-ORDER-LEVEL-OVERLAP because no catalog operation exists to perform an order-id-level join (work item W-WI-OVERLAP-JOIN-BLOCKED).

What was released: the data-gathering/diagnostic scope (query_order_late_status on DA-ORD, query_release_batch_log on DA-WMS, query_pickup_delay_log on DA-PICK) and the attempted-but-blocked order-level cross-reference. The originally requested customer-facing chatbot (generate_customer_delay_explanation, target SH-CX, i.e. CL-01) was NOT released, because it is blocked by the open VOB-U-ORDER-LEVEL-OVERLAP.

The release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION with no holds: the diagnostic findings are released as-is, but customer-facing cause attribution is withheld until order-level overlap (VOB-U-ORDER-LEVEL-OVERLAP, required BEFORE_RELEASE) and the RELEASE-BATCH root-cause fix (VOB-R-2, required BEFORE_PRODUCTION) are resolved.

A proposed remediation step - formally assigning ownership of diagnosing/fixing RELEASE-BATCH (21/30 failed runs, E-04) to SH-WMS - is recorded as unfinished/not executed because write access to fix the job was unavailable in the available time.
limitations_explained: Order-level overlap between the 290 released-after-pickup orders (E-04) and the 300 handover-late orders (E-01) has not been confirmed - only inferred from numeric proximity (assumption A-ORDER-OVERLAP-ASSUMED) - because no tool exists to join order-db and wms-jobs by order id; this keeps VOB-U-ORDER-LEVEL-OVERLAP open and is why the chatbot cannot ship yet.

The actual mechanical root cause of the RELEASE-BATCH failures (U-RELEASE-BATCH-ROOT-CAUSE, 21/30 failed runs, M-RELEASE-BATCH-FAILURE-RATE=0.7, E-04) is still unknown and unfixed; only an ownership escalation to SH-WMS was feasible, since write access to remediate the job was not available.

VOB-R-2 remains open: there is no confirmation that SH-WMS has diagnosed and fixed the RELEASE-BATCH root cause or reduced the 0.7 failure rate, so the chatbot's cause attribution cannot be relied on in production until this is resolved.

The carrier pickup-delay figure (median 2.0 hours, E-02/E-06) is based on a sample of only 60 of roughly 1000 orders; U-PICKUP-SAMPLE-REPRESENTATIVE (LOW criticality) is still open, so it is unclear whether this sample generalizes to the full order population.

General data completeness and validity of order-db, pickup-log and wms-jobs (U-DATA-COMPLETENESS-VALIDITY, MEDIUM criticality) is still open, which limits confidence in the headline 30% late-rate, 290-order, and 2-hour figures.

The Shop-to-Carrier handoff (H-PICK) has unknown delivery status and semantic validity, which is a procedural gap noted at the DEFINE gate (CONDITIONAL_PASS finding on handoff H-PICK) alongside the deferred overlap item.
output.summary: The customer experience team (SH-CX) requested a chatbot (CL-01) to tell customers why parcels are late. Investigation defined the root problem (PD-1) as a warehouse-side fault: 30% of orders (300/1000) are late at the handover stage (E-01), traced to the RELEASE-BATCH job failing in 21 of 30 runs, with 290 orders released only after carrier pickup (E-04) - not a carrier-scheduling issue (H-CARRIER-PICKUP-SCHEDULING rejected) nor a mere communication gap (H-CUSTOMER-COMM-GAP rejected). The DEFINE gate returned CONDITIONAL_PASS because the critical question of whether the 290 and 300 affected orders are the same population (order-level overlap) could not be verified with available tools and was deferred as VOB-U-ORDER-LEVEL-OVERLAP. As a result, the diagnostic data-gathering scope was released, but the originally requested chatbot was withheld: the release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION, holding the chatbot pending confirmation of order-level overlap and a verified fix to the RELEASE-BATCH root cause (VOB-R-2) before any customer-facing cause attribution goes to production.
